fact_sheet.scam_name: Silent Call AI Voice Cloning Scam
fact_sheet.story_hook: Scammers initiate calls from unknown numbers that remain silent when answered. If the recipient speaks, even a simple 'hello', their voice is recorded and then cloned using Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology. The cloned voice is subsequently used to impersonate the victim and call their family members, fabricating urgent emergencies like accidents or arrests, to coerce them into transferring money quickly.
fact_sheet.red_flag: The key warning sign is receiving a call from an unknown number where no one speaks on the other end, or if the caller does not immediately identify themselves upon answer.
fact_sheet.the_fix: If you receive a silent call from an unknown number, do not speak first. Hang up immediately if the caller does not identify themselves. Always verify any urgent requests for money by contacting the family member directly through a known, alternative contact number. Report suspicious calls to the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) at 997 or the PDRM CCID Scam Response Centre at 03-2610 1559 / 03-2610 1599.

obfuscated_story.title: The Silent Trap: AI Voice Cloning Scams
obfuscated_story.summary: A silent phone call from an unknown number allows scammers to record and clone your voice using AI. These fake recordings are then used to trick your family into sending money for staged emergencies.
obfuscated_story.story: The scam begins with a simple, unsuspecting phone call from an unknown number. When a retiree answers and says 'Hello?', the line remains eerily silent. Unknown to the victim, this brief audio clip is being recorded and processed by high-end Artificial Intelligence (AI) software. Within minutes, the software creates a near-perfect digital clone of the victim's voice. Armed with this clone, the scammer calls the victim's daughter. Using the synthesized voice, the scammer impersonates the victim, sounding frantic and distressed. They claim to be at a police station following a serious traffic accident, pleading for an immediate RM5,000 transfer to a 'legal officer's' account to avoid being detained by PDRM. Panicked by the sound of her own parent's voice, the daughter nearly transfers the funds before realizing the 'legal officer' is pressuring her to bypass standard bank protocols. This sophisticated tactic leverages emotional urgency and technology to bypass traditional skepticism.
obfuscated_story.solution: If you receive a silent call from an unknown number, do not speak first and hang up immediately. If a family member calls from a different number claiming an emergency, hang up and call their known original number to verify the story. Report any incidents to the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) at 997 or the PDRM CCID Scam Response Centre at 03-2610 1559.
red_flags: Calls from unknown numbers that remain silent when you answer
Caller does not identify themselves immediately
Urgent demands for money involving legal trouble or accidents
Requests to transfer money to personal bank accounts instead of official agency accounts
